data.title: Clindamycin + Nicotinamide gel
data.summary: II Antibacterials · Combination: lincosamide antibiotic + vitamin B3 (anti-inflammatory)
data.body:
_Topicals · II Antibacterials_

**Class:** Combination: lincosamide antibiotic + vitamin B3 (anti-inflammatory)

## Mechanism of action
- Clindamycin: 50S protein-synthesis inhibitor (anti-C. acnes)
- Nicotinamide 4%: anti-inflammatory (inhibits neutrophil chemotaxis, IL-8, mast cells), reduces sebum, improves barrier
- Nicotinamide is non-antibiotic, so the combination may reduce reliance on the antibiotic

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Mild–moderate inflammatory acne

## Dose & formulations
- Usually clindamycin 1% + nicotinamide 4% gel once or twice daily; combine with BPO or a retinoid; limit antibiotic use to about 12 weeks

## Adverse effects
- Dryness, irritation, burning

## Contraindications
- As for clindamycin

## Pregnancy & lactation
Acceptable.

## Viva points
- Nicotinamide 4% gel alone is comparable to clindamycin 1% in some trials
- Combination still needs BPO to prevent resistance

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.41 and ch.57 (nicotinamide); Khopkar ch.28 (topical niacinamide). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
